questions.q: Predrag Djordjevic and Stelios Giannakopoulos arrived at Olympiacos together in 1996 from the same Greek club. Which one?
questions.hint: Dusan Bajevic signed both Djordjevic and Giannakopoulos from Paniliakos in 1996, and both went on to win every title of the seven-year run.

questions.q: Olympiacos led 1-0 at Anfield in December 2004 through a curling free-kick, before Liverpool won 3-1 with a late Steven Gerrard strike. Who scored that free-kick?
questions.hint: Rivaldo bent the free-kick into the Kop end to put Olympiacos ahead on 8 December 2004, before Sinama Pongolle, Mellor and Gerrard turned the group tie around and sent Liverpool on their way to Istanbul.

questions.q: Olympiacos' seven-in-a-row ended when they were beaten to the 2003-04 title. Which club took it?
questions.hint: Panathinaikos won the 2003-04 championship, ending Olympiacos' seven consecutive titles from 1996-97 to 2002-03.

questions.q: Predrag Djordjevic played 13 seasons at Olympiacos between 1996 and 2009. How many Greek championships did he collect?
questions.hint: Twelve, from thirteen attempts. Olympiacos won the title every season Djordjevic was there apart from 2003-04, when Panathinaikos pipped them by two points.

questions.q: Olympiacos signed the Brazilian playmaker Giovanni in the summer of 1999. Which club did they buy him from?
questions.hint: Giovanni joined Olympiacos from Barcelona in 1999, three years after the Catalans had signed him from Santos.

questions.q: Olympiacos demolished and rebuilt Karaiskakis Stadium in just 14 months, moving into the new ground in which year?
questions.hint: The rebuilt Karaiskakis Stadium opened in 2004, in time to stage football at the Athens Olympics; Olympiacos' first competitive match there was a 2-1 win over Kallithea on 19 September 2004.

questions.q: Stelios Giannakopoulos won the Greek championship in all seven of his seasons at Olympiacos, from 1996-97 to 2002-03, then left in May 2003 for which Premier League club?
questions.hint: Sam Allardyce signed him on 28 May 2003, a year before he won Euro 2004 with Greece, and he stayed at the Reebok until he was released in 2008.

questions.q: Rivaldo signed for Olympiacos in July 2004. Which club did he join them from?
questions.hint: Rivaldo joined Olympiacos on 22 July 2004 from Cruzeiro, where he had spent only around two months after leaving AC Milan.

questions.q: In February 1981, 21 fans were crushed to death leaving Karaiskakis Stadium after Olympiacos' 6-0 win over AEK Athens. Which gate gave the tragedy its name?
questions.hint: The crush on 8 February 1981 happened at Gate 7, where a half-closed exit door trapped fans rushing out to celebrate. Olympiacos' main supporters' association still carries the name Gate 7 in memory of the 21 who died.

questions.q: Before taking charge at Olympiacos in 1996, Dusan Bajevic had already won four Greek championships as manager of which club?
questions.hint: Bajevic won four league titles at AEK Athens between 1989 and 1994 before crossing to Olympiacos, where he won three more in a row and later added the 2004-05 championship.

questions.q: Olympiacos won the 2024 UEFA Europa Conference League final 1-0 against Fiorentina with a header in the 116th minute. Who scored it?
questions.hint: Ayoub El Kaabi headed in Santiago Hezze's cross in the 116th minute at the Agia Sophia Stadium in Athens, making Olympiacos the first Greek club to win a European trophy.

questions.q: Olympiacos reached the Champions League quarter-finals in 1998-99, losing 2-1 away and drawing 1-1 at home to go out 3-2 on aggregate. Which club knocked them out?
questions.hint: The Delle Alpi leg settled it — Juventus held on in Athens, then went out themselves in the semi-final, beaten 4-3 on aggregate by Manchester United.

questions.q: Rivaldo left Olympiacos in 2007 after three league titles and signed immediately for which club, a move that did not go down well in Piraeus?
questions.hint: Rivaldo joined AEK Athens on a free transfer on 29 May 2007 straight from Olympiacos, having won the Greek championship in each of his three seasons at the club.

questions.q: Olympiacos' run of seven straight championships began in 1996-97, and one manager delivered the first three before leaving in November 1999. Who was he?
questions.hint: Dusan Bajevic crossed from AEK Athens in June 1996 and won the 1996-97, 1997-98 and 1998-99 titles - the first of them Olympiacos' first championship in ten years. He departed in November 1999, and a succession of coaches carried the run on to a seventh title in 2003.

questions.q: Giovanni spent six seasons at Olympiacos, from 1999 until 2005. How many Greek league titles did he win there?
questions.hint: Giovanni won five championships with Olympiacos — 1999-2000, 2000-01, 2001-02, 2002-03 and 2004-05 — missing out only in 2003-04, the season he finished as the league's top scorer with 21 goals.
